headline: Cyclone Murasu is forecast to hit Andhra Pradesh as a severe storm on 3 Nov. Doha talks on the Iran war show little movement as tankers burn near Hormuz, and Russia launched 433 drones at Ukraine on 1 Nov.

signals.name: US equity stress
signals.summary: US stocks near highs and volatility contained despite the energy shock
signals.state: US markets were closed over the weekend; the S&P 500 last closed on 30 Oct about 3% below its 52-week high, with the VIX at 19.4, just under the 20 Watch line. The coming week brings the 3 Nov US midterms and the 5 Nov Bank of England decision.
signals.for_you: Conditions in US equities are calm by historical standards. Volatility near 20 means sharper daily swings are plausible if energy or rate news worsens.
signals.rubric_hit: VIX < 20 and S&P 500 drawdown from 52-week high < 5%.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — S&P 500 (^GSPC)
Yahoo Finance — VIX (^VIX)

signals.name: FTSE 100
signals.summary: FTSE 100 within 2% of its high, supported by energy and mining shares
signals.state: The FTSE 100 last closed on 30 Oct at 10,730, about 1.7% below its 52-week high. Its heavy weighting to oil, gas and mining companies has cushioned it from the energy shock. London markets reopen on 2 Nov, ahead of the Bank of England decision on 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: The index's resilience reflects its global, commodity-heavy make-up rather than the domestic UK economy, which faces higher energy bills and rising rates.
signals.rubric_hit: Drawdown from 52-week high < 5% and no single-day fall > 2.5% this week.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — FTSE 100 (^FTSE)

signals.name: Bond market volatility
signals.summary: Treasury volatility at the Watch line as yields hover near 5%
signals.state: The MOVE index of Treasury volatility stood at 100 on 30 Oct, right on the Watch threshold, with the US 10-year yield at 4.93% after touching about 5.2% in mid-October. The Fed held on 28 Oct after a September hike, and markets price a December hike. No trading since 30 Oct.
signals.for_you: Long-term borrowing costs, including US mortgage rates, are elevated and moving more than usual. This feeds through to global bond markets, including UK gilts.
signals.rubric_hit: MOVE 100–140, or US 10y moved ≥ 40bp in a month, or weak auctions flagged.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — ICE BofA MOVE Index
FRED — 10-Year Treasury yield (DGS10)
investingLive — FOMC decision 28 Oct: rates left unchanged

signals.name: Credit spreads
signals.summary: High-yield spreads tight at 3.3% — no sign of a credit crunch
signals.state: The US high-yield option-adjusted spread was 3.26% at the latest reading (29 Oct), well inside the 4% Watch line and little changed over the month. Lenders are not yet demanding a meaningful premium for corporate default risk despite higher rates and energy costs.
signals.for_you: Companies can still borrow on easy terms. A sharp widening would be an early sign of stress spreading from energy into the wider economy.
signals.rubric_hit: US HY option-adjusted spread < 4.0%.

sources.title: FRED — ICE BofA US High Yield OAS (BAMLH0A0HYM2)

signals.name: US dollar
signals.summary: Dollar index steady around 102
signals.state: The DXY dollar index was 102.0 at the 30 Oct close, up about 2% over three months, within the normal range. Fed hikes have supported the dollar without the violent moves that squeeze dollar borrowers abroad.
signals.for_you: Currency conditions are orderly. A stronger dollar would raise the sterling cost of oil, which is priced in dollars.
signals.rubric_hit: DXY moved < 5% over 3 months and is between 90 and 108.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — US Dollar Index (DX-Y.NYB)

signals.name: Banking system stress
signals.summary: Financial stress index below zero; 2026 bank failures have all been small
signals.state: The St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index was −0.58 in the latest weekly reading (week to 23 Oct), below its long-run average. Six small US banks have failed in 2026, the largest (Nano Banc, 25 Sep) with about $736m in assets; no new failure was reported as of 1 Nov.
signals.for_you: There is no sign of systemic banking stress. Commercial property refinancing at higher rates remains the pressure point for smaller lenders.
signals.rubric_hit: St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index < 0, ECB CISS < 0.25, and no notable bank failures or rescues.

sources.title: FRED — St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index (STLFSI4)
Disruption Banking — Six US banks failed in 2026, the most in a decade

signals.name: Gold (fear gauge)
signals.summary: Gold off its highs at about $3,900 as real yields rise
signals.state: Gold futures last traded at $3,899 (30 Oct close), about 6% lower over three months. The fall despite the Gulf war is consistent with rising US yields and Fed hikes, and gold is not signalling financial panic.
signals.for_you: Gold's fall suggests markets see the energy shock as an inflation and rates problem rather than a financial-system crisis.
signals.rubric_hit: 3-month change between −8% and +10%.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — Gold futures (GC=F)

signals.name: Crypto stress
signals.summary: Bitcoin 10% below its high; no stablecoin or exchange stress reported
signals.state: Bitcoin traded around $77,800 at 11:40 UTC on 1 Nov, about 10% below its 52-week high and well inside the 25% Watch line. No major stablecoin de-peg or exchange failure has been reported as of 1 Nov.
signals.for_you: Crypto markets are not currently a source of wider financial stress.
signals.rubric_hit: Bitcoin drawdown from 52-week high < 25% and no major stablecoin/exchange incidents.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — Bitcoin USD (BTC-USD)

signals.name: US recession risk
signals.summary: US economy grew 3.4% in Q3; recession indicators quiet
signals.state: The advance estimate on 29 Oct showed US GDP grew at a 3.4% annualised rate in Q3. The real-time Sahm rule indicator is 0.00, far from the 0.5 recession trigger, and the 10y–2y curve is positive at +0.38. October payrolls are the next test.
signals.for_you: Recession risk in the US looks low for now. The main risk to growth is the combination of high energy prices and rising interest rates.
signals.rubric_hit: Sahm rule indicator < 0.30 and no negative GDP quarter in the latest two releases.

sources.title: Axios — U.S. economy races ahead with 3.4% growth in third quarter
FRED — Real-time Sahm Rule indicator

signals.name: US inflation
signals.summary: US CPI at 4.0%, pushed up by the oil shock
signals.state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7% in August, as energy prices fed through, within the 3–4.5% Watch band. The Fed raised rates in September and held on 28 Oct, with markets pricing another hike in December. October CPI is due mid-November.
signals.for_you: Higher US inflation keeps global interest rates elevated, which affects borrowing costs well beyond the US.
signals.rubric_hit: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.

sources.title: FRED — CPI for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL)
investingLive — FOMC decision 28 Oct

signals.name: Euro-area economy
signals.summary: Euro area grew 0.4% in Q3, but France contracted and October PMIs slowed
signals.state: Eurostat's flash estimate on 30 Oct showed euro-area GDP up 0.4% in Q3, though French output contracted. October flash PMIs (23 Oct) showed expansion weakening, and the ECB warned on 29 Oct that energy prices pose downside risks to growth. Neither stagnation nor a sub-50 PMI is yet confirmed.
signals.for_you: Europe is still growing, but the energy shock is beginning to bite. A slowdown there would weigh on UK exports.
signals.rubric_hit: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.

sources.title: Agence Europe — Euro area GDP estimated to have risen by 0.4% in third quarter
ECB — Monetary policy decisions, 29 October 2026

signals.name: China economy
signals.summary: China's factory PMI slipped to 49.3 in October after 4.5% Q3 growth
signals.state: The official NBS manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1 in September, below the 50.0 consensus (released 31 Oct), and services also contracted. Q3 GDP grew 4.5% year on year, within the official range, so growth is not yet clearly below target and there is no sign of financial contagion.
signals.for_you: China is not currently a source of global shock, though weak domestic demand keeps it reliant on exports and trade relations.
signals.rubric_hit: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.

sources.title: Trading Economics — China NBS manufacturing PMI
Investing.com — China Q3 GDP grows 4.5%

signals.name: Central bank stress
signals.summary: Central banks caught between energy-driven inflation and slowing growth
signals.state: The Fed hiked to 3.75–4% in September and held on 28 Oct in a 10–2 vote; the ECB held at 2.50% on 29 Oct, warning of upside inflation and downside growth risks. The Bank of England decides on 5 Nov, with a hike widely expected. Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma across the G7.
signals.for_you: Interest rates are more likely to rise than fall in the near term in the US and UK, which affects mortgages, loans and savings rates.
signals.rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.

sources.title: ECB — Monetary policy decisions, 29 October 2026
investingLive — FOMC decision 28 Oct: rates left unchanged
Trading Economics — UK 10-year gilt yield

signals.name: Sovereign debt stress
signals.summary: French borrowing costs spike: OAT–Bund spread near 160bp
signals.state: France's 10-year spread over German Bunds was about 159bp on 30 Oct, above the 150bp Alert line, after peaking above 170bp on 22 Oct (Teleborsa). French GDP contracted in Q3 and street protests entered a third weekend on 31 Oct. UK 30-year gilts are near 5.7%.
signals.for_you: Rising government borrowing costs tend to feed into mortgage and business lending rates, and can force tax rises or spending cuts.
signals.rubric_hit: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.

sources.title: Ideal Investisseur — OAT–Bund spread
Borsa Italiana/Teleborsa — OAT spread over Bund above 170bp

signals.name: Global activity (PMI)
signals.summary: Global PMI strong in September, but October flashes and China's PMI softened
signals.state: The J.P.Morgan Global Composite PMI rose in September to its joint-highest level since 2021 (published 6 Oct). October readings so far point to softer momentum: euro-area flashes slowed (23 Oct) and China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 (31 Oct). The October global figures are due 2–4 Nov.
signals.for_you: Global activity has held up well so far despite the energy shock.
signals.rubric_hit: J.P.Morgan Global Composite PMI > 51.

sources.title: S&P Global — Global PMI hits joint-highest since 2021
Trading Economics — China NBS manufacturing PMI

signals.name: Oil (Brent)
signals.summary: Brent above $110 as Hormuz stays largely closed
signals.state: Brent last settled at $113 on 30 Oct, above the $110 Alert line and up 11% over the month. Iran said four tankers caught fire after striking mines near Hormuz on 31 Oct, and Iran halted tanker movements the same day. In Doha talks Tehran has offered to reopen the strait within two days, on conditions the US has not accepted.
signals.for_you: Expect continued high petrol, diesel and heating-oil prices, with knock-on effects on transport costs and inflation.
signals.rubric_hit: Brent > $110, or 1-month change > +30%, or a major physical supply outage (> 2 mb/d).

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — Brent crude futures
Al Jazeera — Iran FM says US outreach a 'positive step' as delegation in Qatar
Khaleej Times — Iran war live updates, 31 October

signals.name: European gas (TTF)
signals.summary: TTF above €100/MWh; EU storage lowest for the time of year on record
signals.state: Dutch TTF gas last traded near €104/MWh (30 Oct), up from about €28 in January, after Qatari LNG deliveries to Europe stopped in May. EU storage was 74.6% full on 24 Oct against 82.9% a year earlier, the lowest for the date since 2011 (IEEFA). Hormuz talks in Doha had produced no reopening as of 31 Oct.
signals.for_you: UK and European energy bills are set to rise sharply this winter. A cold winter would add further pressure on supply.
signals.rubric_hit: TTF > €70/MWh, or a major supply cut-off (e.g. Qatar LNG or Norway outage > 1 week).

sources.title: Euronews — European natural gas prices soar
Yahoo Finance — Dutch TTF gas futures (TTF=F)

signals.name: Shipping chokepoints
signals.summary: Tanker attacks near Hormuz on 29–30 Oct; Red Sea route still contested
signals.state: Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after striking mines near Hormuz on 31 Oct, and Iran reported four such fires that day; Oman rescued 25 crew from a burning vessel on 30 Oct. Ship attacks near the strait hit a record in October. Iran's terms for reopening, discussed in Doha on 31 Oct, include sanctions relief and recognition of its routes.
signals.for_you: Disrupted shipping lanes raise fuel and goods prices and lengthen delivery times. FCDO advice applies for travel to the Gulf region.
signals.rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran FM says US outreach a 'positive step' as delegation in Qatar
Khaleej Times — Iran war live updates, 31 October

signals.name: Container freight
signals.summary: Container rates above $4,400/FEU despite a 3% weekly fall
signals.state: Drewry's World Container Index fell 3% to $4,429 per 40ft container on 29 Oct, still above the $4,000 Alert line; Shanghai–Los Angeles was $7,514 and Shanghai–New York $9,631. Gulf disruption and rerouting keep capacity tight. The next WCI reading is due 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: High shipping costs typically feed into prices of imported goods with a lag of a few months.
signals.rubric_hit: WCI > $4,000/FEU, or > +60% in a month.

sources.title: Shipping Telegraph — Drewry WCI decreased 3% (week 44)

signals.name: Global food prices
signals.summary: FAO food index at 136, up 5.8% on a year
signals.state: The FAO Food Price Index rose 1.5% in September to 136.0, 5.8% above a year earlier and above the 135 Alert line (published 8 Oct). Cereals rose 5.1% and sugar 6.1%, driven by Black Sea logistics, dry weather and Hormuz shipping uncertainty. The October figure is due in the first week of November.
signals.for_you: Food inflation is likely to stay elevated. Import-dependent poorer countries are most exposed.
signals.rubric_hit: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.

sources.title: MercoPress — FAO Food Price Index rises in September
FAO — Food Price Index

signals.name: Critical minerals
signals.summary: China's rare-earth export pause expires 10 Nov; helium squeeze persists
signals.state: China's suspension of some rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov, with no renewal announced as of late October. The loss of Qatari helium through Hormuz, plus China's July helium export ban, has created shortages for chipmakers; the US has designated helium a critical material. No production stoppages outside China have been confirmed.
signals.for_you: Shortages of specialist materials can raise costs and delay electronics, vehicles and defence equipment.
signals.rubric_hit: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.

sources.title: Technology.org — China's rare-earth export pause: what ends on 10 November
Value Chain Asia — TSMC helium shortage

signals.name: US–China / Taiwan
signals.value: No major PLA exercise since Dec 2025
signals.summary: Routine PLA activity; leaders' dialogue continues ahead of APEC
signals.state: Beijing has held no large-scale exercise around Taiwan since December 2025; the Liaoning carrier group drilled in the Philippine Sea on 14–15 Oct before heading to the South China Sea (USNI). Taiwan says it is watching for larger drills as the season peaks. No new exercise had been reported as of 1 Nov.
signals.for_you: No acute Taiwan Strait crisis is under way. Watch for a sudden 'snap' exercise, which Beijing used in December 2025.
signals.rubric_hit: Managed relations; dialogue channels open; routine PLA activity.

sources.title: USNI News — Chinese carrier strike group heads to South China Sea
Focus Taiwan — Taiwan watching for large-scale PLA drills

signals.name: Russia–NATO
signals.summary: Drone ship sinkings off Bulgaria and airspace violations on NATO's flank
signals.state: Ukraine says Russian drones sank four cargo ships just outside Bulgarian waters in October, and Romania blamed Russia for a ship sunk by drone (23 Oct). Russian jets have entered Polish, Lithuanian and Estonian airspace, and EU intelligence agencies warn of sabotage plots against defence firms (Al Jazeera, 29 Oct). No Article 4 request as of 1 Nov.
signals.for_you: Direct conflict is not under way, but incidents are rising. Follow official advice if travelling near NATO's eastern borders.
signals.rubric_hit: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Russia's alleged sabotage campaign in Europe raises fears of escalation
CEPA — Russian strikes rise across NATO's eastern flank

signals.name: Iran nuclear programme
signals.summary: No IAEA access amid war; talks focus on inspections as strike plans reported
signals.state: The IAEA reported Iran to the UN Security Council on 1 Oct and has no access to Iranian sites. On 31 Oct Iran's security chief said Tehran was debating whether to keep its ban on nuclear weapons, and state TV said nuclear talks could only follow US acceptance of Iran's demands. Rubio said Trump had not decided whether to resume strikes.
signals.for_you: Renewed strikes would likely push oil and gas prices higher again.
signals.rubric_hit: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran FM says US outreach a 'positive step' as delegation in Qatar
Khaleej Times — Iran war live updates, 31 October

signals.name: Korean peninsula
signals.summary: North Korea fires about 10 ballistic missiles amid DMZ landmine row
signals.state: North Korea fired about ten short-range ballistic missiles from near Wonsan on 29 Oct, its 17th launch of 2026. A joint South Korea–UN probe found North Korea planted the mines that injured three South Korean soldiers in the DMZ on 21 Sep; Pyongyang denies it. No further launch was reported to 1 Nov.
signals.for_you: Tension is elevated but there has been no direct clash between forces.
signals.rubric_hit: Ballistic or cruise missile launches, or troop deployments abroad.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — North Korea fires missiles as row over landmine blast intensifies
The Japan Times — North Korea fires off around a dozen ballistic missiles

signals.name: Trade war & tariffs
signals.summary: US tariffs reset under Section 301; new Russia-linked tariff powers signed
signals.state: After the Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs on 20 Feb, the US moved to 10–12.5% Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies from 24 Jul; the average effective rate was 7.1% in August (Yale Budget Lab). China's pause on some rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov with no renewal announced, a possible new flashpoint.
signals.for_you: Tariffs are lower than in 2025 but policy remains unpredictable, and new threats could quickly change trade costs.
signals.rubric_hit: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.

sources.title: Penn Wharton Budget Model — Effective tariff rates, updated 14 Oct
Technology.org — China's rare-earth export pause: what ends on 10 November

signals.name: Sanctions & coercion
signals.value: US blockade of Iran; Graham Act in force
signals.summary: US blockade of Iran and new secondary-sanction powers on Russia
signals.state: The US naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in force; on 31 Oct Iran set the lifting of sanctions imposed after the Islamabad memorandum and release of frozen funds as conditions in Doha talks. The Lindsey Graham Act, signed in October, expands secondary sanctions on Russia's trading partners. No new major package was announced to 1 Nov.
signals.for_you: Sanctions are reshaping energy trade routes and can affect prices and supply far from the targeted countries.
signals.rubric_hit: Major new packages, secondary-sanction threats on large economies, or asset-seizure moves.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran FM says US outreach a 'positive step'
Debevoise — Lindsey Graham Act expands US sanctions and tariffs

signals.name: Political instability
signals.summary: No G20 government has fallen this month; France's budget fight is the one to watch
signals.state: No G20 government has fallen and no coup was reported as of 1 Nov. France saw a third weekend of social protests on 31 Oct, with about 320,000 marchers by the Interior Ministry's count and 27 arrests by mid-afternoon (Euronews). The US holds midterm elections on 3 Nov.
signals.for_you: Political risk is building rather than acute. A French government collapse would likely push its borrowing costs higher.
signals.rubric_hit: No G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in the past month.

sources.title: Euronews — France's third weekend of social protests
Khaleej Times — US midterm elections 2026 explainer

signals.name: Russia–Ukraine
signals.summary: Russia launched 433 drones overnight on 1 Nov; Kyiv under emergency power cuts
signals.state: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 433 drones overnight into 1 Nov, 371 of which were downed, with hits at 16 locations; Kyiv introduced emergency power cuts after attacks on energy infrastructure. A drone strike on Dnipro's main station on 29 Oct killed at least 13 civilians (UN). Front lines changed little.
signals.for_you: Follow FCDO advice against all travel to Ukraine. Strikes on energy infrastructure may affect European power and gas markets this winter.
signals.rubric_hit: Significant escalation — major new offensive, mass-casualty strikes, a nuclear-plant safety incident, or new state involvement.

sources.title: Ukrainska Pravda — Russia attacks Ukraine with 433 drones overnight
Korabelov — Kyiv faces emergency power outages

signals.name: Israel, Gaza & region
signals.summary: US–Iran war in tense stalemate; Qatari mediators back in Tehran
signals.state: The war that began with US–Israeli strikes on Iran on 28 Feb continues at lower intensity, with a US blockade and mine and fire incidents near Hormuz (30–31 Oct). Saudi-led forces intercepted drones over Riyadh and the Eastern Region on 31 Oct. Iranian negotiators were in Doha on 31 Oct; Al Jazeera's correspondent reported no notable flexibility in Iran's position.
signals.for_you: Follow FCDO travel advice for Israel, Lebanon, Iran and the Gulf states, where conditions can change quickly.
signals.rubric_hit: Multi-front escalation, major cross-border strikes between Israel and its neighbours, or mass-casualty events.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran FM says US outreach a 'positive step' as delegation in Qatar
Khaleej Times — Iran war live updates, 31 October

signals.name: Sudan
signals.summary: Record drone attacks on civilians in October; army rejects talks
signals.state: Strikes on a market and homes in RSF-held Nyala on 26 Oct killed more than 100 people according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers; medical groups gave lower figures. The UN says drones are now the leading cause of civilian deaths. A senior RSF commander, Siddiq Ander, announced his defection on 31 Oct. About 14 million people are displaced.
signals.for_you: Sudan is the world's largest displacement crisis. Aid agencies report severe funding shortfalls.
signals.rubric_hit: Major sieges or massacres reported, or famine spreading to new areas.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — RSF senior commander defects
The National — Sudanese trapped between drones and incarceration, says UN mission

signals.name: DR Congo (east)
signals.value: Kivu clashes; no city changed hands
signals.summary: Fighting persists in the Kivus; US sanctions Rwanda's defence ministry
signals.state: Clashes between the M23-led alliance and pro-government forces continued in North and South Kivu in late October, including fighting in the Kalehe hills, with no major city changing hands as of 1 Nov. On 28 Oct the US sanctioned Rwanda's Ministry of Defence for supporting the rebellion.
signals.for_you: The conflict affects supply of minerals such as coltan and tin used in electronics.
signals.rubric_hit: Active fighting or a fragile ceasefire.

sources.title: Critical Threats — Congo War Security Review
Washington Post — US sanctions Rwanda over M23

signals.name: Sahel insurgency
signals.summary: JNIM fuel blockade on Bamako persists; insurgency pressing toward Guinea
signals.state: JNIM's fuel blockade of Mali's capital, imposed in September 2025 and declared total on 28 Apr 2026, was last reported in force with Bamako relying on escorted convoys; no report of it being lifted was found as of 1 Nov. Mali air strikes reportedly killed 89 civilians on 19 Oct, and JNIM is expanding toward Guinea.
signals.for_you: Follow FCDO advice against all travel to most of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger.
signals.rubric_hit: Blockade or fall of a capital or major city, or mass-casualty attacks spreading to coastal states.

sources.title: The OpsCon — Bamako still moves on escorted fuel convoys

signals.name: Myanmar
signals.value: Civil war; no major city changed hands
signals.summary: Civil war grinds on; junta relies on air strikes after failed Rakhine offensive
signals.state: Fighting continued in Arakan, Sagaing, Shan and Chin in late October: the Arakan Army reported sinking two junta vessels near Sittwe on 26 Oct, and resistance media reported a junta air strike on Sittwe that killed 11 civilians on 23 Oct (unverified). No major city has changed hands this month.
signals.for_you: Follow FCDO advice; much of Myanmar is unsafe for travel.
signals.rubric_hit: Civil war at sustained intensity.

Mizzima — 29 October

signals.name: India–Pakistan
signals.summary: Border shootings and Line of Control firing keep tensions elevated
signals.state: Indian border guards shot dead two people on the Punjab border on 2 Oct, and both countries summoned diplomats (Al Jazeera, 3 Oct). No cross-border military strikes have occurred since the 2025 clashes, and no new LoC incident was reported to 1 Nov.
signals.for_you: Follow FCDO advice for areas near the India–Pakistan border and Line of Control.
signals.rubric_hit: Ceasefire violations, a major terrorist attack with blame assigned, or treaty suspensions.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Pakistan, India summon diplomats after border killings

signals.name: Nuclear risk
signals.summary: No arms-control treaty since New START lapsed; testing threats unresolved
signals.state: New START expired in February 2026 with no replacement, leaving no US–Russia limits for the first time in decades. Trump has threatened to resume nuclear testing, and on 31 Oct Iran's security chief said Tehran was debating whether to keep its ban on nuclear weapons. No test or alert-level change has been reported.
signals.for_you: Nuclear use remains very unlikely, but the guard-rails that made it predictable are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
signals.rubric_hit: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.

sources.title: Arms Control Association — Trump, Xi, Putin failing to tackle nuclear threat

signals.name: Atlantic hurricanes
signals.summary: No Atlantic storms; none expected in the next 7 days
signals.state: The National Hurricane Center's outlook on 31 Oct showed no active systems and no formation expected in the next seven days; nothing new was reported to 1 Nov. The season officially ends on 30 November.
signals.for_you: No hurricane threat to the Caribbean or US at present.
signals.rubric_hit: No hurricane active, or none threatening land within 5 days.

sources.title: NHC — Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook

signals.name: Pacific & Indian cyclones
signals.summary: GDACS red alert as Cyclone Murasu heads for Andhra Pradesh landfall on 3 Nov
signals.state: GDACS raised a red alert on 1 Nov for the Bay of Bengal system FOUR-26, now named Cyclone Murasu. IMD expects it to become a severe cyclonic storm and cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur by the morning of 3 Nov, with winds of 100–110 km/h gusting to 120 km/h. Typhoon In-Fa near Japan remains at green alert.
signals.for_you: If you are in or travelling to coastal Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, follow IMD and local authority warnings and FCDO travel advice. Expect flight and rail disruption around landfall.
